evals.name: check-mirrors-the-venv-walk-and-the-closest-config
evals.expected_output: Routes to check (the default action) and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table covering the Bash floor, jq, the Ruff binary resolved by the hook's repo-managed .venv walk then PATH, the governing consumer Ruff config, the ruff_format_enabled toggle, and hook registration — one remediation line per FAIL, nothing modified.
expectations: Resolves Ruff the way the hook does — the exact .venv interpreter paths it tests for the current platform, walking up from the edited file toward the repo root, then PATH — and does not PASS a binary the hook would not accept
Reports the config walk as stopping at the FIRST (closest) governing config found walking toward the repo root, honoring Ruff's own same-directory precedence
Counts a pyproject.toml only when it carries a [tool.ruff] section or a [tool.ruff.*] subtable such as [tool.ruff.lint], reading the hook for the exact section test
Reports missing jq as FAIL and states the consequence: the hook skips with a visible once-per-session notice instead of formatting

evals.name: no-ruff-config-is-the-opt-out-not-a-defect
evals.prompt:
/ruff-format:setup check

No Ruff config anywhere in the repo and Python files are never formatted. Is the plugin broken?
evals.expected_output: Answers no: the opt-in walk found no governing config, so absence is the opt-out by design and the plugin is inert — reported as INFO, not FAIL — matching the README's "ships no rules of its own" stance.
expectations: Classifies the missing config as INFO (inert by design), never FAIL, and states the plugin is not broken
Does not offer to repair the state, and creates a minimal Ruff config only when explicitly asked
Does not report a missing Ruff binary as a FAIL in this state — the FAIL is conditioned on a Ruff config governing the repo
Notes that a pyproject.toml without a [tool.ruff] section or subtable does not count as the opt-in

evals.name: install-target-confirmed-in-project-and-recorded-through-the-manager
evals.prompt:
/ruff-format:setup apply install-ruff

We use Poetry here.
evals.expected_output: Does not install blind: Poetry defaults its environment to a cache directory while the hook resolves only repo-ancestor .venv interpreters or PATH, so an in-project environment is confirmed from the tool's own config first; when confirmed, Ruff is recorded through Poetry's own dev-dependency add so the manifest and lockfile carry it, never a bare pip install. Otherwise it guides rather than installing somewhere the hook never looks.
expectations: Confirms in-project mode from the tool's own config or environment answer before installing, rather than assuming the environment location
States the constraint that drives it: the hook resolves repo-ancestor .venv interpreters or PATH, nothing else
Records through the manager's dev-dependency add command, and explains that a bare pip install into a managed environment is state the tool's next sync or clean silently removes
Never creates or mutates an environment: with no environment yet it uses the tool's record-only mode where one exists and hands the sync step to the consumer
Stops with guidance anchored on the astral install URL when no environment plus no recognized manager, or conflicting signals, make the target ambiguous
After the remediation, re-runs the relevant check probe and reports its actual result rather than claiming resolved on the install command's exit code

evals.name: repeat-apply-changes-nothing
evals.prompt:
/ruff-format:setup apply

Everything passed on the last run. Go again.
evals.expected_output: Re-runs check, finds no FAIL, reports "already configured", and makes no change on the second pass.
expectations: Runs check first even on the repeat invocation
Reports "already configured" and performs no write
Does not re-add ruff through the repo's dependency manager and does not re-touch its manifest or lockfile when the binary already resolves
Does not prompt interactively — the action was given in the invocation

evals.name: bare-apply-neither-installs-nor-picks-rules
evals.prompt:
/ruff-format:setup apply

Ruff isn't installed and we have no config. Install it globally and write us a config.
evals.expected_output: Declines both: bare apply installs nothing (install-ruff is the explicit argument that authorizes it), a global install is never in scope, and a minimal Ruff config is offered only when explicitly asked because the plugin imposes no rules of its own.
expectations: Does not install Ruff from bare apply — states that install-ruff is the explicit argument that authorizes it
Refuses a global install and refuses to create a virtual environment, installing only into a managed environment the repo already uses
Does not write a Ruff config unless explicitly asked, because the plugin imposes no rules of its own
Never installs system packages and never writes Claude Code user settings, pluginConfigs, or the plugin cache

evals.name: headless-toggle-off-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt:
/ruff-format:setup apply

I'm on a CI box with no interactive session — how do I turn the hook off?
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless change to a plain `claude plugin install ruff-format@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config ruff_format_enabled=false` rerun, states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value (verified on Claude Code 2.1.240), rules out uninstalling to reconfigure, and ends by rerunning check and reporting the observed effective value.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install … --config ruff_format_enabled=false` rerun, naming this plugin's own key and the false value the request asked for

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option to its manifest default

Carries the CLI version the --config-against-an-installed-plugin claim was verified on — the literal 2.1.240 — and scopes it to a non-sensitive option at user scope, noting a sensitive option and project/local scope were not covered
Notes that -s defaults to user, so the scope `claude plugin list` reports must be passed and a project/local scope needs the command run from that project's directory
Ends by rerunning check and reporting the OBSERVED effective toggle value rather than asserting the change took effect
